### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**7** anchor(s) derived from **3** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/types/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/types/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **45** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 49c8e0f069ac5e21b11ba40d8bbbbfd8cd2eced2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fff61c8965c504ca31343878e68d75202e1f8386` — the merge of head `7305a38f6529d0c6464f4efc9e2bb1ee0b590596` into base `49c8e0f069ac5e21b11ba40d8bbbbfd8cd2eced2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fff61c8965c504ca31343878e68d75202e1f8386 && git checkout fff61c8965c504ca31343878e68d75202e1f8386
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 49c8e0f069ac5e21b11ba40d8bbbbfd8cd2eced2 7305a38f6529d0c6464f4efc9e2bb1ee0b590596 && git checkout -B drift-repro 49c8e0f069ac5e21b11ba40d8bbbbfd8cd2eced2 && git merge --no-ff 7305a38f6529d0c6464f4efc9e2bb1ee0b590596

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 49c8e0f069ac5e21b11ba40d8bbbbfd8cd2eced2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `4cac717c4a0ecdbfa24b64b15b1946f7126e6bb7`
Local-runs: probe — `flowRuntimeStateOf` (types, head blob) and cloud's `flowRuntimeStateFrom` (cloud head blob) run side by side under node 22 strip-types over 14 engine shapes (one row off/on, two rows, no row, no `enabled`, string `enabled`, null row, non-array, async read, throwing read, no method, undefined, null, `this`-bound read): 0 differences
Scope: objectstack-ai/objectstack PR #37147 (Part of #36856), base `origin/main` 1f3e9f68, two commits 83e30667 (fix) and 4cac717c (changeset declaration only, one line); 8 files: `packages/types/src/flow-runtime-state.ts` + test + index export, `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-authoring.ts` + test, `packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts` + 35442 test, one changeset
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

### ① Derived judgments

- **`runtimeState` only for flows.** The arm reads `type === 'flow' && getAutomation`, where `type` is `canonicalTypeOf(input.type)`, so `flows` reads the same switch (pinned) and every other type never calls the engine (pinned: an object item, `reads() === 0`). Holds.
- **After the read gate.** The engine is read only after `stored` exists and `itemGate` returned a non-refuse verdict; a 404 and every refusal return before the read, and no refusal envelope carries the key. The order is also not load-bearing for disclosure: `GET /automation/_status` already serves every flow's `enabled` bit to any authenticated caller (the #7900 audit note in `automation.ts`), and this door additionally needs `metadata:write` + `manage_metadata`. No new disclosure.
- **Answer-shape consumers.** The key is added, never replaces; order is `type, name, draft, [version], runtimeState, item`. `git grep` of `get_metadata_item` across `packages/`, `ui/`, `skills/`, `packages/qa`: no code parses this answer except the door's own tests; `ui/` holds only i18n labels for `describe_metadata`. Cloud does not consume this door's answer. Nothing breaks.
- **Same reading as `/automation/_status`.** Both call the engine's synchronous `getFlowRuntimeStates()` (`engine.ts`, body in `flow-definitions.ts`) and filter by `name`; the toggle door's read-back already uses the exactly-one-row rule this PR copies. Lookup path: `_status` resolves through `deps.getService(context, 'automation')` (= `resolveService(requestKernel, name)` with no scope id); the reader resolves through `deps.resolveService(context, 'automation', context.environmentId)`, the same call one line up that resolves the `protocol` the item itself is read from. On a `kernel-resolver` host both legs answer from the request's own kernel first (#22944), so env A's engine cannot answer env B's flow; on a shared-project host the reader takes the scoped engine first, which is the stricter of the two. Item and switch come from one environment.
- **Two holders → undefined.** Right. The engine emits one row per slot under the bare name (`flowSlotName`, ADR-0150 D4), and this door has no package address to pick a slot by; the toggle door answers the same case the same way (echo, never a guessed row). Absent reads as unknown, never "enabled", which is the safe direction for the card's failure (an agent saying a switched-off approval runs).
- **Wording of `enabled: false`.** `isFlowEnabled` is `flowStatusDisabled` (status `obsolete`/`invalid`) OR `flowLedgerDisabled`, and the ledger side includes a packaged flow shipped off with no admin row (`defaultActive: false`, #34655). The tool description says "`false` means an admin switched it off" (R2).

### ② Semver level

- Declarations: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` (new `@objectstack/types` root exports; new answer key; nothing refused, no input key added) and `Metadata-protocol: none` (nothing a metadata author can write changes). Both correct.
- Rule verified verbatim in objectstack `AGENTS.md` § Post-Task Checklist step 3 (origin/main 1f3e9f68, lines 1029–1031): "The level follows the kind alone: a kind takes at least **`minor`** on a package the diff moves, `none` takes **`patch`**; a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`". With kind `none`, `patch` on `@objectstack/types`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/mcp` is what the rule prescribes. Not breaking, so no ADR-0087 marker or migration is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No `packages/spec` change, no authorable key, no governed surface, no `ui/` change. `Governed Surface Queue Guard` green.
- New cross-package seam lives in `@objectstack/types`, the package all three readers already depend on (the stated reason in the module header); no new dependency edge.
- Text seam to cloud: `packageDocAnswerRule` is used verbatim by cloud's build door, and cloud's e2e/unit tests compare against the function's own output rather than a literal, so the next pin carries the sentence without breaking cloud.

### ④ Design judgment

Sound. The switch is engine state, not definition, so carrying it beside `item` rather than writing it into the item is right; placing it ahead of `item` and answering unknown as absent are both the conservative choices. Factoring the reading into `@objectstack/types` so the open door, cloud's door and the answer-order text share one key and one rule is the right altitude. The one gap is that the production assembly of the port is not pinned (R1).

### Findings

- **R1 (should fix, non-blocking): the shipping wiring has no failing pin.** Every new runtime test builds `createOpenAuthoringRegistry` with an injected `getAutomation`. Deleting the `getAutomation` entry from `resolveOpenAuthoringInjection` (or dropping its `context.environmentId`) leaves all 55 tests green and the feature silently off. The fixture at `mcp-authoring.test.ts` ~L212 already fakes `resolveService` by name; one case answering `'automation'` (and asserting the env id it was asked with) through `resolveOpenAuthoringInjection` would pin both delivery and the per-env lookup. Failure mode today is fail-safe (no key = pre-fix answer), hence non-blocking.
- **R2 (should fix, non-blocking): the tool description over-attributes.** `get_metadata_item`'s description says `runtimeState.enabled: false` "means an admin switched it off". The engine's `enabled` is also `false` for a packaged flow shipped off with no admin row (#34655) and for status `obsolete`/`invalid`; an agent relaying the description will tell a user an admin did something no admin did. `packageDocAnswerRule`'s own sentence ("switched off and does not run") is accurate; align the description to it.
- **R3 (note): ablation covers the answer, not the gate order.** The recorded ablation deletes the spread (2 red). Moving the engine read above the gate would only be caught on the 404 path (`reads() === 0`); since a refusal never carries the key, that is no leak, so no pin is owed, but the PR body's "read only after the gate" is a code-comment guarantee, not a tested one.

Checks against the brief:
- (4) Tests/ablation: flow off/on, plural spelling, none/two rows, non-flow and 404 never read the engine, no automation port, rule sentence present/absent are each pinned; the types reading has its own 4 cases. Ablation (spread deleted) reported 2 failed/53 passed and restored blob == HEAD. Gap: R1.
- (5) CI: at 83e30667 (tree differs from head only in one changeset line) 57 success / 11 skipped / 0 failed. At head 4cac717c: see the CI line below.

CI-at-head: all 72 check runs at 4cac717c have finished: 59 success, 13 skipped, 0 failed. Test Core 10/10, Test UI 16/16, Type Check UI, Type Check workspace/consumer/debt gates, every Lint lane, Check Changeset and PR-body guards are all green.
